title: Sprint 1 — Build a Restaurant Menu Page (HTML Only)
description: Your first real web project. You will build a complete restaurant menu page using only HTML, no CSS or JavaScript. The goal is to master semantic structure — headings, sections, lists, tables, images, and forms — so your pages are meaningful, accessible, and well-organised.

tickets.title: Ticket 1 — Page Header, Navigation & Hero Section
tickets.description: Lay the foundation of the restaurant page. Build the `<header>` with the restaurant name in an `<h1>`, a `<nav>` with anchor links to each section on the page, and a hero `<section>` with a tagline and an address paragraph.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Header & Navigation
tasks.description:
Create a `<header>` containing:
- An `<h1>` with the restaurant name (e.g. 'Bella Cucina')
- A `<nav>` with an unordered list of anchor links: `#menu`, `#about`, `#contact`

All links must use the `href` attribute pointing to the correct section IDs.

tickets.title: Ticket 2 — Menu Section with Tables & Lists
tickets.description: Build the heart of the page — the actual menu. Use semantic HTML elements like `<section>`, `<article>`, `<table>`, and `<ul>` to organise starters, mains, and desserts.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Starters & Desserts (Lists)
tasks.description:
Inside `<section id="menu">`, create two `<article>` elements:
1. An article for 'Starters' with an `<h3>` and an unordered list (`<ul>`) of at least 4 starter items, each in a `<li>` with the dish name and price.
2. An article for 'Desserts' with the same structure.

Each `<li>` must show both the item name and price as text.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Mains Table
tasks.description:
Inside the menu section, create a third `<article>` for 'Main Courses' with a `<h3>` heading and a `<table>` with columns: Dish, Description, Price.

Requirements:
- Use `<thead>` with `<th>` elements for the header row
- Use `<tbody>` with at least 5 `<tr>` rows of main course data
- Every cell must use proper `<td>` tags

tickets.title: Ticket 3 — About Section, Gallery & Contact Form
tickets.description: Complete the restaurant page with an About section, an image gallery using figures, and a contact/reservation form with proper labels and input types.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Reservation Contact Form
tasks.description:
Create `<section id="contact">` with a `<h2>` and a `<form>` for table reservations. The form must include:
- Name: `<label>` + `<input type="text">`
- Email: `<label>` + `<input type="email">`
- Date: `<label>` + `<input type="date">`
- Number of Guests: `<label>` + `<input type="number">`
- Special Requests: `<label>` + `<textarea>`
- A `<button type="submit">Book Table</button>`

All inputs must have matching `id` and `for` attributes on their labels.
